plaintext: A printer on Oak Street kept the presses running after dark whenever a ship brought fresh paper. He mixed the ink himself and checked each sheet against the copy the editor had marked. Customers wanted notices of auctions, lists of timber prices, and the names of passengers who had booked a cabin. The apprentice learned to lock the type tightly so the lines would not dance. When the last form was washed the room smelled of oil and wet rag paper, and the printer walked home along the canal with ink still on his cuffs.
